name: Captured Light: From Pinhole to Pixel
description: The camera obscura, the silver plate, roll film and the pixel: how people learned to hold light still and then to make it move.

checkpoints.name: Before the photograph
checkpoints.note: Ancient thinkers noticed that light through a tiny hole forms an upside-down picture. Ibn al-Haytham explained the optics, artists used the camera obscura, and Niepce finally fixed an image on a plate.

checkpoints.name: Silver and glass
checkpoints.note: Daguerre's daguerreotype was announced in 1839 and amazed the public with its detail. Fox Talbot's negatives on paper allowed many prints, a method that became the standard.

checkpoints.name: Film for everyone
checkpoints.note: Eastman's Kodak put cameras in ordinary hands. Edison's Kinetoscope and the Lumieres' projector turned photographs into moving pictures, and Melies took viewers to the Moon.

checkpoints.name: Sound and colour
checkpoints.note: The Jazz Singer brought speech to film, Kodachrome and Snow White brought colour, instant cameras gave pictures in minutes, and colour television carried them into living rooms.

checkpoints.name: Digital light
checkpoints.note: The digital camera replaced film with sensors. Photoshop made editing routine, Toy Story was made wholly by computer, and Flickr and Instagram turned photographs into a daily way of talking.
